chapter: Donaldsonville, family and Richard M. Jones
title: Creole country and the Black Devils band
summary: Jones did not speak French; he describes the Black Devils band and its players versus Williams's society band.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Did you speak any French growing up? No.
Uh-huh. I didn't talk no French.
Yeah, but I know that people from around that area did speak French, yeah.
Well, yeah, that's Creole section. Did you ever hear of the Black Devils band? That's the band that... That's an old band out there. You know who come out of that band?
Leo Sanjay. Oh, yeah? That's from...they're from...they're from...they're from Plagma.
Uh-huh. And what was he playing then?
Banjo. Banjo. Leo Sanjay...they had a trumpet player from the poor end of the world called Clown Smugglers. Clown what? Clown Smuggler.
That must not have been his right name. Uh-huh. That was his last name.
Smuggler. What's Smothers? That's M-O-T-T-R-L. Oh, Smothers.
Clown Smothers, yeah. Oh, yeah. I see, and I misunderstood you. I was pronouncing it wrong. It was Clown Smugglers. Yeah, I see. But that was a good band, the Black Devils.
Yeah, they had a nice jazz band, but then they was in the category with Clermont Williams.
More barrel bands, I guess, aren't they?
Yeah, there was more jazz. Clermont had the society band. Uh-huh.
